punchline: Epictetus, a man with no legal freedom, became one of history's great teachers of freedom.
thirty_sec: Epictetus was born a slave and lame for much of his life, yet became a leading Stoic teacher. An ancient story says that when his master twisted his leg until it broke, he only said, 'Didn't I tell you it would break?' Whether or not it's true, it captures his teaching: some things are up to us, our judgments and actions, and most things aren't. Freedom comes from focusing on the first.
question: What are you worrying about right now that isn't actually up to you?
key_contrast: Up to you, not up to you
